clue.text: Flirtatious type Gladys managed, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A woman named Gladys pulled off a little flirting, in part.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladies' man is a man who enjoys flirting with and charming women, a flirtatious type.

clue.text: Female's contribution to mass production

definitions.meaning: a woman's first name, standing for any female
the hymn of praise sung as one section of the Latin Mass setting

explanation.definitionFit: Gloria is a woman's name and also the 'Glory to God' movement of a sung Mass.

clue.text: Become annoyed and take the lead in court?

definitions.meaning: on a tennis court, to go one set ahead of the opponent

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase as GET UP (go ahead by) a SET, as in tennis scoring; the question mark flags the punning sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To get upset is an idiom for becoming annoyed; in tennis, being 'up a set' means leading.

clue.text: Leader of expedition on rocky ridge becoming more nervous

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so take the start of expedition
rocky means unsteady or shaken, so the letters of ridge are jumbled

explanation.surface: The head of a climbing party grows jumpier on an unstable mountain ridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets the leader above the jumbled ridge in this down clue; 'becoming' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy is a colloquial synonym for nervous or tense, so edgier is its comparative.

clue.text: Farm building unlikely to collapse

definitions.meaning: a building on a farm where horses are housed

explanation.definitionFit: A stable houses horses, and as an adjective stable means steady and secure.

clue.text: Flight in first airship

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A trip aboard the very first airship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests air travel, matching the airship, but it is a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a set of steps between floors, another word for a staircase.

clue.text: Information needed before writing German article

definitions.text: Information needed before writing German article

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
der is the masculine form of 'the' in German

explanation.surface: Before you can choose the right German word for 'the', you must know something about the noun.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: in German the choice of der, die or das depends on the noun's grammatical class, which you must know first.
explanation.definitionFit: German articles change according to a noun's grammatical class, masculine, feminine or neuter, so that knowledge comes first.

clue.text: Academic book

definitions.meaning: a British university lecturer ranking just below a professor
a book of selected texts, especially one for learners

explanation.walkthrough: In British universities a reader is a senior academic post, just below professor.
explanation.definitionFit: A reader is both a senior British university teacher and a textbook of selected passages.

clue.text: Dud clues he replaced with new, not as originally planned

indicators.note: replaced means put back in a different place, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A setter swaps out weak clues for fresh ones, departing from the plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' shuffles DUD, CLUES and HE together with N for 'new' into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unscheduled was not on the timetable, so it was not part of the original plan.

clue.text: East European army ordered to seize a central part of Hungary

indicators.note: to seize means to grab and hold, so one piece takes the others inside it
ordered means arranged anew, so the letters of army are rearranged
the central part of a word is its middle letter, here of Hungary

explanation.surface: A Hungarian army is told to capture the middle of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' turns ARMY into MYAR; 'to seize' puts A plus G, the middle letter of Hungary, inside it: M-AG-YAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A Magyar is a Hungarian, a member of the main ethnic group of Hungary in Eastern Europe.

clue.text: Relating to main disturbance of a lunatic

indicators.note: a disturbance throws things into disorder, so the letters of a lunatic are jumbled

explanation.surface: A madman causes trouble at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is the poetic word for the open sea, not an adjective meaning chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical means concerning the sea or sailing, and the main is an old poetic term for the sea.

clue.text: Performs, oddly enough, in concert

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and seventh, of performs

explanation.surface: Someone plays in a concert, which is somewhat strange.
explanation.walkthrough: A prom is a promenade concert, as in the BBC Proms held each summer in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A prom is a promenade concert, an orchestral concert where some audience stand.

clue.text: Families creating pièces de résistance

indicators.note: making pieces of a word breaks it up, so the letters of resistance are rearranged

parts.note: the French word, accents aside, has the letters of resistance

explanation.surface: Lineages are produced by chefs' showpiece dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creating pièces de' asks for pieces of 'résistance', its letters broken up and reassembled.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestries are lines of descent, which is one sense of families or lineages.

clue.text: Basis for scoop — guts shown by politician, as seen in other rows

parts.note: guts are one's innards or insides
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A journalist's exclusive rests on a politician spilling his guts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown by' joins the pieces; 'as seen in other rows' appears to point to a feature of the grid's other rows and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An inside story is confidential information from an insider, the kind of material a newspaper scoop is built on.

clue.text: Casual female making appearance in one routine

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: something making an appearance in another shows up within it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: routine as an adjective means normal or usual

explanation.surface: A relaxed woman turns up in a set daily routine.
explanation.walkthrough: F goes inside I + NORMAL, giving IN-F-ORMAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal and casual are synonyms describing relaxed dress or manner.

clue.text: Not the first uphill struggle on a trail

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
a scent is a trail followed by hounds

explanation.surface: A hiker plods up a steep path again.
explanation.definitionFit: A reascent is a second climb, so it is an uphill struggle that is not the first one.

clue.text: House assembled, with voting system key — excellent!

parts.note: PR stands for proportional representation, an electoral system
E is a musical key
fab is slang for fabulous or excellent

explanation.surface: Someone builds a house, gets electoral reform and a key, and is delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces; in Britain prefabs were factory-made houses put up quickly after the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a prefabricated house, one assembled on site from parts made in a factory.

clue.text: Destitution of writer — why are you reportedly upset?

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards
reportedly says these words are only heard, so they become the letters that sound them

parts.note: the three words sound like the letters Y, R and U, as in text-speak

explanation.surface: A poor author is asked why they are so distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' says the three words are heard as three letter names, as in text-speak; 'upset' turns that string upside down in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Penury is extreme poverty, which is what destitution means.

clue.text: Money doesn't grow on trees — but this does in the Pacific

definitions.text: Money doesn't grow on trees — but this does in the Pacific

parts.words: Money doesn't grow on trees — but this does in the Pacific
parts.note: money is slangily bread, and the clue points to a tree crop of the Pacific islands named partly for that slang word

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is turned round: bread is slang for money, and a Pacific tree bears a fruit named for its bread-like flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pacific tree whose large starchy fruit tastes like bread when baked, hence the name.

clue.text: One part of deck on ship

parts.note: a means one
a deck is made up of planks or boards

explanation.surface: A single plank of the deck is on the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboard means on or in a ship, aircraft or other vehicle.

clue.text: First-class spinner following gratuitous advice?

indicators.note: following places this piece after the other

parts.note: a tip is a gratuity and also a piece of advice, so both senses give the word
a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: An excellent spin bowler comes after some unsolicited advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts the spinner below the advice in this down clue; 'gratuitous' plays on gratuity, the other sense of the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiptop is an informal word meaning excellent or of the highest quality.

clue.text: Beer with creamy head, such as Guinness

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of creamy

explanation.surface: A pint with a creamy head, like a glass of Guinness stout.
explanation.walkthrough: Guinness is not the stout but the actor Sir Alec Guinness.
explanation.definitionFit: Alec is a first name, and the actor Sir Alec Guinness is one example of a person so named.

clue.text: Certainly not on track, with one of the two fellows missing

indicators.note: missing says a piece is left out of the phrase

parts.note: off course means having strayed from the intended route
F is the abbreviation for fellow, and the phrase has two of them

explanation.surface: Something has definitely strayed from its route, minus one of a pair of companions.
explanation.walkthrough: OFF COURSE has two Fs; dropping one leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Of course is a phrase meaning certainly or naturally.

clue.text: Vehicle for economic improvement

definitions.meaning: a light truck with an open back
a recovery in trade or the economy

explanation.definitionFit: A pickup is a small open truck, and a pickup in business is a recovery.

clue.text: Wine receiving top mark in pubs and clubs

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: bars are pubs
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
A is the top grade in marking

explanation.surface: A wine awarded the highest rating in drinking establishments.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside BARS + C: BARS-A-C.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet white wine from the Bordeaux region of France, an example of wine.

clue.text: Down, for example, in number by day's end

indicators.note: by means beside, so this piece comes next

parts.note: a count is a number or total

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here of day

explanation.surface: A tally is completed in time for the close of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Down is a county of Northern Ireland, not a direction; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: County Down in Northern Ireland is an example of a county.
